summary: A constant named MAX_DOCS = 8 capped NOTHING — it only ordered a list. Believing the name re-rolled a settled $11,701 income to $3,129 on the Wilson file.
detail: Renamed to STUB_PRIORITY_WINDOW. Before reasoning from any constant, open its call sites.

summary: EXTRACT_SYSTEM in docFacts.ts had ZERO importers. A YTD fix was written there, shipped, and changed nothing.
detail: READ_ONE_SYSTEM in this file is the only prompt that runs. grep the importers before editing a prompt.

summary: Borrower-specific figures (37,689 / 40,818) were used as an EXAMPLE inside this SHARED prompt. The reader anchored on them and returned the same YTD for two different stubs.
detail: State rules generically. Never put one borrower's numbers in a prompt every borrower is read with.

summary: One employer printed two ways split into two jobs: 'SANTA MONICA COM COLLEGE' vs the same name with its parent district double-counted a salary at $9,932/mo; an IRS transcript's 'EXTR REAC TALE INC' never merged with 'EXTREME REACH TALENT, INC.'
detail: sameEmployerStem (containment) + isAbbrevOf (token truncation). A WRONG merge deletes a real second income — test both directions.

summary: LOGIC_VERSION is GLOBAL. Bumping it invalidated every file's stability cache at once, and the AI read is non-deterministic, so every borrower's settled number could move.
detail: Bump only when the MATH changed. That cache exists because of 'income I verified last week is different this week on the same file'.

summary: $4,898.05/mo of VA compensation sat in a bank statement (VACP TREAS 310) while the file qualified that borrower at $750. Bank statements were only mined for the deposit-AVERAGE method.
detail: A status doc (DD-214/COE) proves income EXISTS. Ask where the money LANDS — Treasury ACH codes name the program.

summary: /api/competitors was in apiProtected but MISSING from config.matcher — fully public until an adversarial review caught it.
detail: Both lists, always. npm run verify:auth proves it in milliseconds.

summary: A cap named like a policy that silently .slice()s data: MAX_DOCS = 4 in credit-liabilities threw away a borrower's 5th credit document with no error and no flag.
detail: Same shape as the income MAX_DOCS. Grep for .slice( next to a MAX_ constant. A guard may TRIM but must always FLAG what it trimmed.

summary: Number(amount)||0 made a BLANK field render the e-signed card authorization as UNCAPPED ('the amounts shown to me') while the LOS displayed 'blanket up to $0'.
detail: blanketAuthText now THROWS below $1 — there is no safe uncapped version of a signed instrument. Found by the pattern hunt, not by a human.

summary: Tradelines .slice(0,60) BEFORE closed accounts are filtered out, so the effective cap on open DTI-bearing tradelines is far below 60, with no overflow flag.
detail: Understated DTI = a borrower approved for a payment they don't qualify for. Filter first, then guard, and always flag the overflow.

summary: Un-fixed TWIN of the credit-liabilities MAX_DOCS=4 bug: .slice(0,4) on uploaded files server-side AND client-side, no overflow reported.
detail: Fixing one instance of a shape is not fixing the shape. Grep for siblings before calling it done.

summary: PostgREST silently caps any .limit() above 1000. stalledFiles.ts pages explicitly; every other caller still asks for 2000-20000 and treats the result as complete — one has a guard (length===2000) that can never be true.
detail: Page explicitly, or assert the returned count. A guard that cannot fire is the ground-truth shape of a false green.

summary: Module-level 'export let' for per-request overflow would leak one borrower's number onto another's response — a serverless instance serves concurrent requests.
detail: Return per-request values from the function. Never park them on module scope.

summary: A bare 'dataset/' in .gitignore matches at ANY depth — it silently excluded scripts/dataset/build.ts, so the miner was written, run, and never committed.
detail: Anchor data-exclusion patterns to the repo root (/dataset/). Then VERIFY with: git check-ignore -v <the file you expect to keep>.
